messages:
maya: heads up — I just saw a big billing spike in us-west1, ~120k extra estimated in the last hour. dashboard: https://console.costs/reports/redwood/us-west1

infra-bot: alert: autoscaler-group/gpu-pool-1 launched 48 nodes in 00:18 due to unschedulable pods (policy fallback to on-demand)

sam: seeing the same. autoscaler events show: 
```
E0704 03:10:21 autoscaler.go:324] no reserved matching pool for selector 'gpu-family=a100-80gb' — fallback=true
```

liam: quick root cause hypothesis: we deployed the allocator label rotation at 02:30 (rename gpu-family -> gpu-type-v2) and some of the reservation templates still select the old label. autoscaler can't match reservation -> falls back to on-demand pool and spins up large instances.

maya: that matches timing. deployment diff: 
```
- labels:
-   gpu-family: a100-80gb
+ labels:
+   gpu-type-v2: a100-80gb
```

zara: costops: we need a rough delta. query I'm running: 
```
SELECT SUM(cost) FROM billing WHERE region='us-west1' AND resource_type LIKE '%gpu%' AND timestamp > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
```

costops: preliminary shows ~118k extra compared to baseline, mostly noncommitted instance lines. tagging shows reservation_id = NULL for those nodes.

sam: can someone run `kubectl get nodes --selector='gpu-family' -o wide` and `kubectl get nodes --selector='gpu-type-v2' -o wide` to see mixed fleet?

liam: ran it: only 3 nodes have gpu-family label, 52 have gpu-type-v2. reservation controller expects gpu-family label; it rejected matching so the reserved pool wasn't used.

maya: urgent mitigation: revert allocator label change to restore previous label alias so reservations can match. Also add an alias mapping in the reservation controller (gpu-type-v2 -> gpu-family) as a temporary shim.

sam: on it — rolling back allocator config in staging now. will roll to prod if green.

infra-bot: deploy started: allocator-v2 rollback (deploy id: d-8734)

zara: billing team — please start a cloud refund request and open a support case citing autoscaler fallback misconfiguration; we should be able to get some credits for the unexpected noncommitted launches. I'll attach the event timeline.

costops: filing ticket with cloud — case #CB-22190. asked for priority review. included autoscaler logs and timestamps.

liam: postmortem notes we should do: 
- add unit test for label rename migration that updates reservation selectors
- make autoscaler avoid immediate fallback: only fallback after 5m of failed matching or when cluster utilization > X
- emit metric `reservation_match_failures_total` and alert on spikes

maya: agreed. also we should run a reconciliation job to retro-tag the 50 on-demand nodes with reservation metadata if any of them were supposed to be covered by a reservation (so cost attribution is clearer).

sam: rollback to prod completed at 03:18 — allocator labels restored. nodes are now being cordoned/drained and replaced where needed.

infra-bot: autoscaler events: fallback rate dropping to normal. new launches stopped.

zara: costops update: cloud acknowledged receipt and requested detailed invoice lines; expect a response in 24-48h. meanwhile hold on any further pool changes in us-west1.

maya: follow-ups: 1) liam to create PR for alias migration + tests, 2) sam to add 5m fallback guard + metric, 3) zara to track cloud refund, 4) maya will run final cost delta check in 6h and loop in finance.

liam: will open PR today and ping eng-releases for backport to stable branches.

costops: final note — tagging and reservation reconciliation will help with future audits. good catch everyone :thumbsup:
